purpose: Revokes domain or delegated administrator assignments from identities.

fields.name: revokeAssignments
fields.values: non-empty list; 400/INV_INPUT when missing or empty

fields.name: revokeAssignments[].assignmentDomain
fields.values: domain key: PROVISIONING, ROLES, RESOURCES, SECURITY

fields.name: revokeAssignments[].isAllPermissions
fields.values: true removes a domain administrator; false removes a delegated administrator and then each of their granular permissions in that domain

notes: Not called (write). Dashboard sends the selected rows as-is. Gated by the ADMIN_ASSIGNMENT client setting. The reference body adds arraySize, which the server ignores.

purpose: Lists the administrator assignments (domain and delegated admins) in all domains.

params.name: q
params.values: search on the assignee name; * or empty means all (default *)

params.name: sortColumn
params.values: column key from …/assignments/columns, e.g. assignee, domain, adminType (default assignee)

params.name: filterSearch
params.values: filter handed to the assignment reader (default ALL); an unknown value was ignored on the lab

answer: {adminAssignments:[{assignee, assigneeDn, assignmentType, assignmentTypeKey, adminType, adminTypeKey, comment, domain, domainType, effectiveDate, status}], nextIndex, totalSize, total}
notes: Lab: uaadmin holds both Domain Admin and Delegated Admin rows for Provisioning, etc. Values seen: adminTypeKey DOMAIN_ADMIN / DELEGATED_ADMIN, assignmentTypeKey USER, domainType PROVISIONING/ROLES/RESOURCES/SECURITY, status COMPLETED. Dates are epoch milliseconds. filterSearch=bogus gave the same rows as ALL.

purpose: Lists the administration domains the signed-in user is domain administrator of.
notes: A Security domain admin gets every domain; otherwise only the domains the caller administers. Lab (uaadmin): PROVISIONING, ROLES, RESOURCES, SECURITY.

purpose: Lists the columns (with localized labels) of the administrator assignment list.
notes: Keys: adminType, domain, assignmentType, effectiveDate, status, comment, assignee, expirationDate — these are the sortColumn values for the list.

purpose: Makes an identity a domain administrator or delegated administrator of a domain.

fields.name: assigneeDn
fields.values: DN of the user/group/container being made administrator

fields.name: adminType
fields.values: DOMAIN_ADMIN or DELEGATED_ADMIN (keys as the list returns them)

fields.name: assignmentType
fields.values: assignee kind, e.g. USER (list shows assignmentTypeKey)

fields.name: domain
fields.values: domain key PROVISIONING, ROLES, RESOURCES, SECURITY; DELEGATED_ADMIN in a domain that does not support delegation (SECURITY) is refused

fields.name: assignee
fields.values: display name; dashboard fills it from the picked identity

answer: the posted node echoed back with status set to a localized success/failed text
notes: Not called (write). Missing assigneeDn/adminType/assignmentType/domain each raise their own validation error. Dashboard turns its picked assignee [{name, dn}] into assignee + assigneeDn. Gated by ADMIN_ASSIGNMENT client setting. The vendor reference shows an XML example.

purpose: Lists all administration domains.
notes: Same four keys as adminDomains on the lab, but this one is not filtered by the caller's rights. The dashboard does not call it.

purpose: Removes granular permissions from a delegated administrator.

fields.name: permissions[].dn
fields.values: DN of the object (role, resource, SoD, PRD, configuration) or container the right applies to

fields.name: permissions[].objClass
fields.values: object class from GET …/admin/permission authObjects[].objectClass: nrfRole, nrfResource, nrfSOD, nrfConfiguration, srvprvRequest, srvprvAppConfig

fields.name: permissions[].permission
fields.values: permissionKey from GET …/admin/permission, e.g. nrfAccessViewRole, nrfAccessCreateResource

answer: list of per-permission success/failed nodes (id = permission dn)
notes: Not called (write). Same body as the PUT. The reference example shows the catalog permission node (id, name, permParams…); the server only uses dn, objClass and permission.

purpose: Grants granular permissions on objects to a delegated administrator.

fields.name: permissions[].dn
fields.values: DN of the object (role, resource, SoD, PRD, configuration) or container the right applies to

fields.name: permissions[].objClass
fields.values: object class from GET …/admin/permission authObjects[].objectClass: nrfRole, nrfResource, nrfSOD, nrfConfiguration, srvprvRequest, srvprvAppConfig

fields.name: permissions[].permission
fields.values: permissionKey from GET …/admin/permission, e.g. nrfAccessViewRole, nrfAccessCreateResource

notes: Not called (write). nrfRole permissions are handled specially (role-level DNs). An empty body returns no response at all.

purpose: Removes the signed-in user's own role/resource/PRD permission assignments (self-revoke).

fields.name: assignments[].instanceId
fields.values: required for resources: the assignment instance GUID from the user's assignment list

notes: Not called (write). Acts on the caller's own assignments only. Inherited assignments (not directly assigned) and non-removable ones are refused with their own messages.

purpose: Would check which of the listed permissions the signed-in delegated administrator may configure.
notes: The method exists in the catalog jar, but its class is not in the catalog application's registered service list, so the path is never served (404 with any body). Use GET …/admin/permission/rights?objectType= instead (that is what the dashboard calls).

purpose: Lists every DirXML driver in the driver set with its GUID.
notes: No parameters (the dashboard builds q/nextIndex/size but never sends them). GUID is upper-case hex. Lab: 4 drivers (DCS, MSGW, Role and Resource, User Application).

purpose: Lists the drivers whose entitlements the caller may bind to resources (resource-mapping drivers).

params.name: type
params.values: driver mapping type as an integer (default 2 = resource mapping); dashboard sends 4 for the CPRS (permission reconciliation) list; a non-number gives 404

notes: Lab has no entitlement-enabled drivers, so every type (0-5) answered {nextIndex:0}. Each driver is also checked for the caller's ENTITLEMENT BIND right.

purpose: Returns a driver with its entitlements (types, views/logical systems, parameter types) for resource mapping.

params.name: cprsSupported
params.values: true keeps only CPRS-capable entitlements (default false)

fields.name: id
fields.values: driver DN (JSON name id; empty body gives 489)

fields.name: requestFrom
fields.values: when set, entitlements without resource mapping are skipped

answer: {id, name, entitlements:[{id, displayName, description, entitlementType, views:[{displayName, viewID, queryKey}], paramTypes}]}
notes: Lab drivers have no entitlements: the answer is just {id, name}. Entitlements whose configuration is missing or not resource-mapping-enabled are left out.

purpose: Lists code-map values of several entitlements for one logical system (view), unpaged.

fields.name: entitlements
fields.values: entitlements whose values to list; each needs id and paramLogicSystem (its view id)

notes: Without paramLogicSystem the server fails with 489 'Error occurred retrieving data from Provisioning Param Code Map table'. With it the lab answered {} (no code maps). Not used by the dashboard (it uses listV2).

purpose: Paged variant: lists code-map values of entitlements that have a logical system (view).

params.name: query
params.values: search text; * or empty for all (default empty)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.values: entitlements whose values to list; each needs id and paramLogicSystem (its view id)

notes: Dashboard uses this when the entitlement has views (it sends hasLogicalSystem:true, which the server ignores). Same 489 as /list when paramLogicSystem is missing; with it the lab answered nothing.

purpose: Lists every code-map value of a driver's (or one entitlement's) resource-mapping entitlements, unpaged.
answer: {entitlementValues:[{id, value, name, description, entitlementName}], arraySize} or {}
notes: Lab answered {}. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Paged list of an entitlement's code-map values when it has no logical system.
notes: Dashboard sends {id: entitlement DN, hasLogicalSystem:false}. Lab: {nextIndex:0, arraySize:0}.

purpose: Lists the values of one code-map view.

fields.name: viewID
fields.values: view id from …/resources/views or an entitlement's views

notes: Lab answered {} even for its one view. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Shows the User Application driver's state, versions and licence expiry.
answer: {patchLevel, appVersion, driverVersion, buildVersion, driverName, expirationDate, state}
notes: Lab: appVersion 4.10.2.0200, driverVersion 4.8, state Running, expirationDate epoch ms; driverName is the DN of the provisioning root.

purpose: Returns one entitlement's configuration: value type, multi-value, resource mapping, views and parameter types.

params.name: entilementDN
params.values: entitlement DN (note the vendor's spelling, missing the t)

answer: {dn, name, description, multiValue, resourceMappingEnabled, type: NO_VALUE|FREE_FORM|DB|ADMIN|QUERY, entitlementLists, entitlementParamTypes}
notes: Missing or unknown DN answers 204 with no body (lab has no entitlements). type is fixed: FREE_FORM (external, free-form), DB (external with code map), ADMIN (static), QUERY (application query).

purpose: Lists the code-map values of a view, optionally limited to parameter types.

fields.name: viewID
fields.values: view id (a DN is also accepted and turned into its GUID)

fields.name: type
fields.values: parameter types separated by %; null/empty for all

notes: Used by form selection fields bound to a code map (dashboard sends viewID = the field's codeMapKey and type null). Results are cached per view/locale/types. Lab: arraySize 0 even for its one view; an empty body also answers {arraySize:0}.

purpose: Finds the existing resources bound to an entitlement value, or proposes a new one, when mapping an entitlement to a role.

fields.name: entitlements[].parameterValue
fields.values: entitlement value used to find matching resources

fields.name: entitlements[].parameterName
fields.values: value label; becomes entName (and the proposed resource name)

notes: Read-only. Lab has no entitlements; a made-up entitlement DN gave 489 'Internal Error'. When no resource matches, the server proposes an unsaved one built from the entitlement.

purpose: Builds an unsaved draft resource from each entitlement value (name, id under ResourceDefs) for the role-mapping dialog.

fields.name: entitlements[].parameterValue
fields.values: entitlement value used to find matching resources

fields.name: entitlements[].parameterName
fields.values: value label; becomes entName (and the proposed resource name)

answer: {entResourcesList:[{entName, resources:[{id, name, description, driver, entitlements, isExisted:false}]}]}
notes: Despite the dashboard's name createTemporaryResource, the server only builds the draft in memory (isExisted false); nothing is saved — saving happens when the role mapping is posted. Checks the caller's resource CREATE right (403 node otherwise). Worked on the lab with a made-up entitlement.

purpose: Sends a resync event for one identity to the Role and Resource Service driver.

fields.name: dn
fields.values: identity DN; empty or malformed is refused

notes: Not called (write; brief forbids it). Only provisioning administrators may call it. Not in the dashboard bundles. Needs a Role and Resource driver in the driver set.

purpose: Lists the granular permissions that can be delegated in an administration domain, by object type.

params.name: domain
params.values: PROVISIONING, ROLES or RESOURCES (SECURITY is refused: not supported for delegated administration; PRD is refused although the reference names it)

answer: {authObjects:[{objectType, objectClass, permissions:[{permissionKey, permissionLabel}]}], nextIndex, totalSize, total}
notes: Missing domain: 412 'invalid input domain type'. domain=PRD: 412 with reason 'PRD'; SECURITY: 412 'Given Domain type is not supported for Administartion Type'. The reference says ROLES, RESOURCES, PRD, but the dashboard and server use PROVISIONING. ROLES covers objectClass nrfSOD, nrfConfiguration, nrfRole…; RESOURCES nrfConfiguration, nrfResource…; PROVISIONING srvprvAppConfig, srvprvRequest.

purpose: Lists the granular permissions a delegated administrator holds in one domain.

params.name: domain
params.values: PROVISIONING, ROLES or RESOURCES (SECURITY is refused: not supported for delegated administration; PRD is refused although the reference names it)

params.name: filterSearch
params.values: optional filter; the dashboard appends extra filterKey=filterValue pairs

notes: Missing assigneeDn: 412 'invalid input DN value'; missing domain: 412 'invalid input domain type'; PRD refused as above. Lab uaadmin has no granular permissions, so nextIndex -1, total 0.

purpose: Tells whether the signed-in administrator may create roles, resources or SoDs.

params.name: objectType
params.values: role, resource or sod (lower case, exact); anything else answers isAccesible:false; missing gives 412 with a null-pointer text

notes: Field is spelled isAccesible. Lab (uaadmin): role → 'create Role' true, resource → 'create Resource' true, sod → 'create Sod' true; 'Role' (capital) and 'prd' → {isAccesible:false}. Domain admins of ROLES (role, sod) / RESOURCES (resource) get true; delegated admins are checked against their create rights.

purpose: Gives the container DNs that granular permissions of a domain can be scoped to.

params.name: domain
params.values: PROVISIONING, ROLES or RESOURCES (SECURITY is refused: not supported for delegated administration; PRD is refused although the reference names it)

notes: ROLES → RoleDefs, configuration, SoDDefs; RESOURCES → ResourceDefs, configuration, driverset1; PROVISIONING → RequestDefs, User Application Driver. Missing domain: 489 'Internal Error'; PRD 489; SECURITY 412 not supported. The dashboard picks SoDDefs from the ROLES answer for new SoDs.

purpose: Searches resource categories.

params.name: q
params.values: matches key or name; * for all (default empty = all)

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name only (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

params.name: token
params.values: cache token from a previous answer; reuses the cached list

params.name: forceRefresh
params.values: true with a token rebuilds the cache (default false)

notes: Lab: default, helpdesk, system. Category ids are per-installation. nextIndex 0 means no more pages. sortBy=id → 489 'Invalid sort-by column: id'.

purpose: Create a resource (here without an entitlement binding).

params.name: fromEntitlement
params.values: true builds one resource per entitlement (default false)

notes: No entitlement needed: a plain resource is created, and it could be assigned and revoked (status Completed).

purpose: Create a resource category (meant to).
notes: 489 'Unable to find abstract layer object definition for the specified definition key.': the server looks up the directory abstraction layer entity 'resources-category', which this installation does not define. Nothing was created (GET /catalog/resourceCategories unchanged: default, helpdesk, system). There is no REST route to delete a category.

purpose: Lists resources bound to a given driver, with filters.

params.name: entitlementId
params.values: only resources bound to this entitlement DN

params.name: resourceType
params.values: dynamic or static (dashboard derives it from a boolean)

params.name: logicalSystem
params.values: only resources for this view/logical system

params.name: managedBy
params.values: true keeps only resources managed by the permission-reconciliation (CPRS) service (default false)

answer: {nextIndex, arraySize, resources:[{id, name, description, driver, entitlementValues, managedBy}]}
notes: Lab has no driver-bound resources, so arraySize 0. The dashboard also sends sortBy/sortOrder/column, which the server does not read.

purpose: Searches resources (v1 list; the dashboard uses listV2 instead).

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name or description (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

params.name: column
params.values: columns to return; default from the user's column preference, else name, description

answer: {nextIndex, arraySize, resources:[{id, name, description, allowMultiple, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions}], totalSize, total}
notes: Lab: 6 resources, all helpdesk system resources. Only domain or delegated resource admins (else 489 security). sortBy=driver → 489.

purpose: Delete resources.
notes: Afterwards POST /catalog/resources/resource answers 489 'Permission with id […] does not exist.'.

purpose: Returns full details of one or more resources (v1).
answer: {arraySize, resources:[{id, name, description, categories, subContainer, approvalOverRide, approvalRequired, approvalIsStandard, revokeRequired, revokeEqualsGrant, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions, managedBy}]}
notes: Read despite the POST. Only resource domain/delegated admins. The dashboard uses resourceV2 instead.

purpose: Change one resource.
answer: the full resource after the change: {id, name, description, subContainer, approval…, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions, managedBy, isExpirationRequired}
notes: Localized name/description for the request locale follow the new values.

purpose: Assign a resource directly to identities.

fields.name: dn or dns
fields.values: resource DN, or a list in dns

fields.name: recipientType
fields.values: user, group, container; not checked here

fields.name: effectiveDate / expiryDate
fields.values: epoch ms as strings; a past expiry is refused

notes: Completed within 12 s (statusCode 50) for a resource with no entitlement; POST /catalog/resources/resource/assignments {dn} shows it with its instanceGuId.

purpose: Revoke a resource from identities.

fields.name: instanceGuId
fields.values: not needed: the revoke worked without it

notes: Unlike DELETE /access/assignments/list, no instance id was needed; the assignment list was empty 12 s later.

purpose: Changes the entitlement binding of an existing resource.
notes: Not called (write). Missing body: 400 payload required.

purpose: Lists the entitlement values bound to a resource.
answer: {entitlementValues:[…]} or {} when the resource has none
notes: Lab helpdesk resources have no entitlements: {}. An empty body gives an HTML 500.

purpose: Same as entitlements/list, typed by entity.
notes: Lab: {}. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Returns full details of resources, including dynamic parameters (what the dashboard uses).
answer: {arraySize, resources:[{id, name, description, categories, subContainer, approvalOverRide, approvalRequired, approvalIsStandard, revokeRequired, resourceParameters, allowMultiple, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions, managedBy}]}
notes: Read. Allowed for resource admins, or inside a workflow session. Adds resourceParameters and allowMultiple compared to v1.

purpose: Change several resources in one call.
Checks proposed resource names: whether the resulting id already exists, and a usable suggested name.

fields.name: resourceNames
fields.values: list of {name}; a top-level name alone gives 489

notes: Invalid characters are stripped/replaced in suggestedName ('Group/Access' → 'Group_Access'); names over 64 characters are cut. The existence check looks for the id in the default resource container, so even existing System resources ('Helpdesk-Group') answered isNameExist false. Not called by the dashboard bundles.

purpose: Lists the code-map views (logical systems) available for entitlement values.
notes: Lab: one view, 'Helpdesk Entitlement'. viewID is per-installation.

purpose: Searches role categories.

params.name: q
params.values: matches key or name; * for all (default empty)

notes: Lab: default, system.

purpose: Searches roles (v1 list; the dashboard uses listV2).

params.name: roleLevel
params.values: role level number(s), comma separated, e.g. 10,20; a non-number gives 489

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name, description or roleLevel (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

params.name: column
params.values: columns to return; default from the roleList column preference, else name, description

answer: {nextIndex, arraySize, roles:[{id, name, description, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions}], totalSize, total}
notes: Lab: 10 system roles, all level 20; categoryKeys=system finds them, default finds none. Only role domain or delegated admins (else 489). sortBy=level → 489 'Invalid sort-by column: level'.

purpose: Remove resource mappings from a role.

fields.name: mappedResources[].entityKey
fields.values: the association DN from POST /catalog/roles/mappedResources/list; without it 489 'Internal Error'

notes: entityKey is what the server deletes by; the mapping list was empty afterwards.

purpose: Map resources to a role.
notes: Creates a resource-association object under cn=ResourceAssociations,cn=RoleConfig,…; POST /catalog/roles/mappedResources/list {id:<role DN>} shows it with status 50 and its entityKey.

purpose: Lists the resources mapped to a role.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name or description (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

params.name: driverID
params.values: only resources of this driver DN (default empty)

fields.name: id
fields.values: role DN; empty body gives 489 'Role id is required'

answer: {nextIndex, arraySize, resources:[{id, name, description, status, mappingDescription, entityKey, driver…}]}
notes: Lab system roles have no mapped resources. The dashboard sends the selected role object and driverID.

purpose: Remove parent roles from a role.
Give a role parent roles.

fields.name: parentRoles[].id
fields.values: parent role DN at a higher level

answer: {success, succeeded:[{id, name}]} or success false with failed[{id, reason, errCode}]
notes: A level-10 parent: 200 success false, errCode 403 'The role belongs to level 10 can't be a parent of any other roles'. The same link shows from both sides (parentRoles/list of the child, subRoles/list of the parent).

purpose: Lists a role's parent roles.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name or description (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

notes: Lab system roles have no parents. Unknown role → 400 'not found'.

purpose: Assign a role directly to identities (no request workflow).
notes: Completed within 12 s: POST /catalog/roles/role/assignments shows 'User Assigned to Role', status Completed, and GET /access/assignments/identities lists the user. The recipient field is subtype (as in the revocation), not type. Revoked with DELETE /access/assignments/list.

purpose: Returns full details of roles (what the dashboard uses).

params.name: entityType
params.values: default role; accepted but not used for roles

fields.name: roles
fields.values: non-empty list; empty gives 489 empty payload

answer: {arraySize, roles:[{id, name, description, categories, level, roleLevel:{name, level, cn…}, subContainer, approvalIsStandard, approvalRequired, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions}]}
notes: A bare {id} (without the roles list) gives 489. Callers without read rights on a system role get 489 'unauthorized to view System Role Details'.

purpose: Change several roles in one call.

fields.name: roles[].name / description / level / categories / owners / approval…

notes: POST /catalog/roles/role showed the new name and description at once.

purpose: Remove child roles from a role.

fields.name: subRoles[].requestDescription
fields.values: required on delete too: else 489 'Request description is required for all Child Roles'

notes: Only role domain administrators (403 otherwise, server code).

purpose: Make roles children of a role.

fields.name: subRoles[].id
fields.values: child role DN, at a lower level than the parent

answer: {success, succeeded:[{id, name}]} or success false with failed[].reason (HTTP 200)
notes: Two level-10 roles: 200 success false 'Invalid roles specified for the role to role assignment … You can only assign role at the different level!'. Worked with a level-20 parent. Read back: POST /catalog/roles/subRoles/list {id:<parent>}.

purpose: Lists a role's child roles with their request details.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name or description (default name); an unknown value gives 489 'Invalid sort order'/'Invalid sort-by column'

answer: {nextIndex, arraySize, roles:[{id, name, description, level, requestDescription, requester, approval}]}
notes: Lab system roles have no children. Dashboard always asks from nextIndex 1.

purpose: Create a separation-of-duties constraint between two roles (meant to).

fields.name: id
fields.values: the new SoD's cn; placed under the SoD container

fields.name: sodApprovalType
fields.values: enumeration names ALWAYS_ALLOW or ALLOW_WITH_WORKFLOW (the server's enum carries '0'/'1' internally; the JSON form is the name)

answer: the SoD with its DN and hasConflicts (server code)
notes: Five variants (sodApprovalType '0', ALWAYS_ALLOW, ALLOW_WITH_WORKFLOW; with and without approvalRequestDef from sods/defaultApprovals, isDefaultApproversUsed and localized names) all gave 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.' with subcode 'Internal exception occurred processing REST service'. Nothing was created (GET /catalog/sods arraySize 0, POST /catalog/sods/sod of the expected DN empty). The duplicate-SoD check before the write wraps any failure in that generic message, so the cause is not visible.

purpose: Returns the default approval settings for new SoDs.
notes: Lab: approvalRequestDef cn=Role Approval,cn=RequestDefs,…; no default approvers or quorum.

purpose: Deletes SoDs.
notes: Not called (write). Each SoD needs the caller's DELETE right.

purpose: Returns details of one or more SoDs.
notes: Read. Lab has no SoDs; unknown ids are skipped (arraySize 0).

purpose: Updates a SoD.

fields.name: id
fields.values: for create: the new SoD's CN (the server puts it under the SoD container); for update: SoD DN

fields.name: sodApprovalType
fields.values: 0 = always allow, 1 = allow with approval workflow

notes: Not called (write).

purpose: Lists the User Application cache holders and their object counts.
notes: Lab: 19 holders.

purpose: Shows the cache cluster (JGroups) name, local address and state.
answer: {clusterName, localAdrress, sentBytes, rcvdBytes, sentMessages, rcvdMessages, isOpen, isConnected, dumpStats} or {}
notes: Lab is not clustered: {}. Field is spelled localAdrress.

purpose: Per-node JVM memory statistics.
notes: Lab: one node.

purpose: JVM memory, runtime, OS and class-loader statistics.
answer: {memoryInfo:{jvmMemoryUsage, jvmMemoryPool, systemMemoryUsage, commitedVirtualMemory}, runtimeStats:[{uptime, startTime, systemProperties:[{key,value}]}], operatingSystemStats, classLoaderStats}
notes: systemProperties lists every JVM system property (about 100), including the trust store's password in clear and key store paths. The method itself checks no rights; on the lab it was called as the applications administrator. Value not recorded here.

purpose: Top CPU-consuming threads and thread-state counts.

params.name: stack
params.values: true adds each thread's stack trace (default false)

notes: stackTrace is one string, not a list.

purpose: Cache holders of the workflow engine.
notes: Lab: same 19 holders as cacheinfo (workflow engine runs in the same JVM).

purpose: JVM memory statistics of the workflow engine nodes.
notes: Same shape as jvmstats.

purpose: Memory/runtime statistics of the workflow engine.
notes: Like memoryinfo, it returns every JVM system property, the trust store's password among them (not recorded here).

purpose: Workflow counts: total, completed, failed, terminated, in progress, recent requests.
answer: {currentTimeStamp, totalWorkflows, completedWorkflows, completedWorkflowsInLast5Mins, …InLast1Min, …InLast10Secs, failedWorkflows, terminatedWorkflows, inProgressWorkflows, newRequestsInLast5Mins, …}
notes: Lab: 20 total, 17 completed, 2 failed, 1 terminated. currentTimeStamp is a server-local text timestamp.

purpose: Top CPU threads of the workflow engine.

params.name: stack
params.values: true adds each thread's stack trace (default false)
